recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Do not remove AUT, Group, or the later participant comments as part of FHIR-18853; those belong to later AdverseEvent decisions and can be audited independently if selected.
issue_request: FHIR-18853 objected that AdverseEvent.contributor's short description sounded like parties involved in causing or experiencing an adverse event, while its definition described contribution of information. The accepted Patient Care resolution replaced contributor with AdverseEvent.participant 0..* BackboneElement, participant.actor 1..1 Reference, and participant.function 0..1 CodeableConcept with example v3 ParticipationType codes.
initial_application: The Jira comment links commit ea5ae1cea9a64a1156a791cb99ae4b4ed7922d06, which changed the legacy AdverseEvent spreadsheet from AdverseEvent.contributor to participant/function/actor and added the adverse-event-participant-function value set. The 2021 source rework preserved that content in source/adverseevent/structuredefinition-AdverseEvent.xml, and source/fhir.ini records the R4-to-R6 mapping from AdverseEvent.contributor to AdverseEvent.participant.actor.
additional_context: FHIR-13894 is the predecessor that renamed eventParticipant to contributor. Later final AdverseEvent decisions refined the same area: FHIR-24684 folded detector into participant and added AUT to the participant-function value set, FHIR-38823 clarified participant versus subject/recorder and removed ResearchSubject actor targets, and FHIR-41402 added Group as a participant.actor target limited to family/household groups. Confluence Patient Care minutes show GF#18853 was deferred in 2018 and discussed again on 2019-09-12; Zulip searches found no direct conflicting thread.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. No source edit was needed because the active AdverseEvent StructureDefinition already has the accepted participant backbone, function, actor, binding, and wording; differences from the 2019 resolution are explained by later approved issues.
